As a Plumber, you will perform the following duties: Performs preventive maintenance to all plumbing and mechanical equipment and parts. Installs, modifies, and repairs plumbing fixtures, bathtubs, showers, toilets, sinks, water fountains, and irrigation. Cleans sewage drain lines.

Repairs and/or replaces potable water lines, water mains, and fire hydrants. Installs and repairs submersible pumps and centrifugal transfer pumps. Performs maintenance on wells, well seals, pumps, storage tanks, and water distribution mains.

Installs and repairs sewer drain systems (e.g., septic tanks, drain fields, sewage lift pumps, and related piping). Serves as a member of the facility's snow response team and participates in snow removal and related activities.
As a condition of employment for accepting this position, you may be required to serve a 1-year probationary period, during which your fitness and whether your continued employment advances the public interest will be evaluated.

This probationary period is an extension of the appointment process and therefore requires the agency to determine if continued employment would advance the public interest, meet the organization goals and mission of the agency, and/or otherwise promote the efficiency of the service.

In determining if your employment advances the public interest, the agency will consider: your performance and conduct; the needs and interests of the agency; whether your continued employment would advance organizational goals of the agency or the Government; and whether your continued employment would advance the efficiency of the Federal service.

Under applicable law, the employment of an individual serving a probationary or trial period automatically terminates when that period ends unless the agency affirmatively certifies, in writing, that the individual's employment should continue and that their appointment should be finalized.

In the absence of agency action to affirmatively certify continued employment beyond the probationary or trial period, such appointments are terminated. Upon completion of your probationary period, your employment will be terminated unless you receive certification, in writing, that your continued employment advances the public interest.

To qualify for this position, you must have sufficient knowledge and ability in the following job-related factors: Ability to do the work of a Plumber without more than normal supervision. (SCREEN OUT) Ability To Interpret Instructions, Specification, etc.

(includes blueprints reading) Ability To Use and Maintain Tools and Equipment Knowledge of Equipment Assembly, Installation Repair, etc.

Technical Practices (theoretical, precise, artistic) Trouble shooting Measurement and Layout If your knowledge and ability in the SCREEN OUT factor above is not sufficient, you will receive no further consideration.

In preparing your application, describe in detail the experience and training which you have had that specifically prepared you for this job and to perform the duties described for this job. Experience should be clearly described and documented in your resume.

The qualifications reviewer will not assume performance of such duties by Job Titles alone. Address your knowledge, skills and/or abilities in the areas shown in the job-related factors.

Volunteer Experience: Experience refers to paid and unpaid experience, including volunteer work done through National Service programs (e.g., Peace Corps, AmeriCorps) and other organizations (e.g., professional; philanthropic; religious; spiritual; community, student, social).

Volunteer work helps build critical competencies, knowledge, and skills and can provide valuable training and experience that translates directly to paid employment. You will receive credit for all qualifying experience, including volunteer experience.

Adjusts regulator pressures, calibrates alarm thresholds, and verifies flow rates at outlets. Coordinates with third-party vendors for annual certification and responds to deficiencies. Follows emergency water supply procedures. Installs, repairs, and maintains plumbing fixtures including water closets, tubs, showers, and sinks. Ensures compliance with building codes and safety standards. Performs other duties as assigned.

Being a Coast Guard civilian makes you a valuable member of the Coast Guard team.

Typical work assignments include: Following sketches, specifications, guides, codes, verbal orders, and supervisory instructions to complete all maintenance, improvement, and repair work associated with water distribution, filtration and plumbing systems, sanitary and storm-water drainage systems and their associated components.

Assembling, installing, maintaining and pressure testing all pipes, fittings, and fixtures of heating, water, drainage, sprinkler, and gas systems according to specifications and plumbing codes.

Carrying out repair, maintenance, or installation of equipment for the generation, utilization, or distribution of heating, ventilation, air conditioning and refrigeration (HVAC) systems. Troubleshooting the sources of plumbing and HVAC malfunctions and completing repairs as indicated or according to work orders.
Applicants will be evaluated on their ability to perform the duties of the position rather than the length of experience. Eligibility will be determined by the relevance, scope, and quality of all experience and training, regardless of where or how acquired.

Applicants will be rated and ranked based on their knowledge of the following job elements: Ability to do the work of the position without more than normal supervision. Ability to interpret instructions and specifications, including blueprint reading. Measurement and Layout. Technical Practices (Theoretical, Precise, Artistic). Troubleshooting.

National Service Experience (i.e., volunteer experience): Experience refers to paid and unpaid experience, including volunteer work done through National Service programs (e.g., Peace Corps, AmeriCorps) and other organizations (e.g., professional; philanthropic; religious; spiritual; community, student, social).Volunteer work helps build critical competencies, knowledge, and skills and can provide valuable training and experience that translates directly to paid employment.

You will receive credit for all qualifying experience, including volunteer experience.

Description de l’entreprise
Ici, le travail parle avant tout le reste. Les chantiers valaisans ont leurs exigences, leurs rythmes, leurs équipes qui se connaissent et une culture du travail bien fait qui ne se raconte pas, elle se vit.
Nous sommes une agence de placement active dans toute la Suisse (28 agences), mais c'est ici, en Valais, que nous cherchons quelqu'un d'ancré. Quelqu'un qui connaît les entreprises locales, leurs façons de travailler, et qui n'a pas besoin d'apprivoiser la région avant d'être efficace.
Pour l'un de nos partenaires établis en Valais, nous sommes à la recherche d'un·e installateur·trice sanitaire.
Description du poste
Du neuf comme de la rénovation, de la planification jusqu'à la mise en service vous couvrez l'ensemble du cycle d'une installation sanitaire.
Planification & organisation
· Étudier les plans d'architecte ou de bureau technique, définir les besoins et calculer les dimensions
· Évaluer les quantités de matériaux, fixer les délais et établir les plans de montage
· Organiser l'approvisionnement, le transport et l'entreposage du matériel sur chantier
Pose de conduites
· Préfabriquer et poser les réseaux d'alimentation eau et gaz, ainsi que les conduits d'évacuation des eaux usées
· Couper, raccorder, souder et fixer les canalisations dans murs, sols et plafonds
· Raccorder l'installation au réseau public, procéder aux essais d'étanchéité et consigner les résultats
· Isoler les conduites contre le bruit, la condensation et l'incendie
· Mettre en service, contrôler et régler la pression
Montage & installation
· Installer lavabos, douches, baignoires, WC, chauffe-eau, adoucisseurs et robinetteries
· Poser des installations solaires thermiques ou photovoltaïques et des systèmes de ventilation
· Assurer le contrôle final et rédiger les rapports de chantier
Entretien & dépannage
· Localiser et réparer les fuites, déboucher, détartrer, remplacer joints, filtres et appareils défectueux
· Intervenir rapidement chez les clients dans le cadre de contrats d'entretien
· Assurer la maintenance des outils et des machines, trier et éliminer les déchets selon les normes en vigueur
Profil recherché
· CFC d'installateur/trice sanitaire
· Expérience solide sur des chantiers en Suisse, idéalement en Valais
· À l'aise aussi bien sur du neuf que sur de la rénovation et du dépannage
· Capable de lire des plans techniques et de travailler en autonomie
· Disponible et réactif — le secteur ne prévient pas toujours avant de tomber en panne
· Bon esprit d'équipe : vous coordonnez régulièrement avec maçons, chauffagistes, carreleurs et électriciens
Nous offrons
Les entreprises avec lesquelles nous travaillons en Valais ont bonne réputation, et ce n'est pas un hasard. Vous intégrez un environnement où le métier est respecté et où votre expérience a de la valeur dès le premier jour.
· Poste fixe avec un salaire à la hauteur de votre expertise
· Perspectives réelles d'évolution et de formation continue
· Un réseau d'entreprises partenaires solides dans la région
· Et bien sûr, vous travaillez là où vous vivez
